public_rationale: Two post-publication papers meet the ordinary emergence reading. Dreamer 4 introduced changes addressing weaknesses in world models. Tiny Recursive Model revised an earlier reasoning method and reported comparative improvements. The second publication completes the stated early-resolution rule. These records support new approaches emerging through research and correction; they do not establish that alternatives displaced LLMs, that GPT-5 caused the developments, or that science invariably corrects itself.
limitations: The evidence consists of preprints and author-reported experiments.
Both methods build on existing research families.
The result depends on reading 'rise' as substantive emergence rather than widespread adoption.
The general philosophical statement about science is not independently proved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Science is self-correcting, and new approaches will rise again from the ashes.

statement.excerpt: The good news here is that science is self-correcting; new approaches will rise again from the ashes.

from_speaker: new approaches will rise again from the ashes
our_interpretation: Read the sentence as predicting that AI researchers will develop substantive new methods that address shortcomings in existing approaches.
Read 'science is self-correcting' as the explanation for that research process, not a separately testable universal guarantee that every scientific error is corrected.
Public methods with comparative experiments can establish emergence. The claim does not require widespread adoption, displacement of LLMs, or achievement of AGI.
An advance can build on an existing research family; 'new' does not require a method without predecessors.
The separate suggestion about AGI arriving in the next decade supplies no deadline for this sentence.
criteria.support_condition: After the post, public research introduces substantive new AI methods, explains shortcomings being addressed, and reports experiments demonstrating the proposed changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event would have to make the predicted emergence impossible. Continued LLM success or a period without qualifying publications would not contradict this open-ended prediction.

evidence.excerpt: a scalable recipe for imagination training
evidence.explanation: Dreamer 4 introduces changes to world-model training addressing inaccurate object interactions and reports an agent obtaining Minecraft diamonds using only offline data. This establishes a substantive new method within an existing research family, without requiring an industry-wide change.

evidence.excerpt: Overall, TRM is much simpler than HRM, while achieving better generalization.
evidence.locator: Section 6, Conclusion; Sections 4–5 describe changes and experiments
evidence.explanation: The Tiny Recursive Model paper revises an earlier recursive method after examining weaknesses in its explanation and design, and reports improved generalization on four benchmarks. Together with Dreamer 4, it establishes multiple new approaches and an observable instance of research correcting earlier assumptions.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Publication of Tiny Recursive Model, following Dreamer 4 on September 29, establishes multiple substantive new methods with comparative experiments addressing documented limitations.
